en: The Mantra for Purifying the Three Karmas from the *Vajrakumāra-dhāraṇī-sūtra*: Oṃ jyeṣṭha-śuddhanaya svāhā.
Join the two palms in the lotus gesture and recite the preceding mantra seven times to consecrate the body, speech, and mind.
All the faults of deluded thoughts are completely purified.
Next, bind the seal for universally prostrating to all Tathāgatas,
with the right knee touching the ground.
The two hands are placed with the left covering the right,
palms facing upward with the backs touching;
the two fingers of faith and the two fingers of wisdom are crossed behind the back and placed upon the crown of the head.
Recite that mantra with the mouth,
abide in this physical posture,
and visualize yourself as pervading the entire dharma-realm.
With one's own body positioned before the two Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, perform the ritual prostration with utmost sincerity while reciting the mantra:
Oṃ vajravidveḥ. Thus, the three karmas are to be operated in unison.
Having paid homage to all the assemblies of noble ones and the images of the maṇḍala deities,
one should immediately assume the full lotus posture (paryaṅka) or the half-lotus posture (ardhaparyaṅka),
and settle the body and mind in meditative composure.
Form the Samaya-mudrā of the Buddha Family:
join the two hands in the lotus-cupped *añjali* gesture,
then open them in the manner of scooping up an object.
Using the two *samādhis* to assist the two recollections at the side of the upper section,
the first text below the two *prajñās* is thus established.
This is the *samaya-mantra* of the Buddha Family.
Recite "Oṃ tathāgatajñānamudrā svāhā" three times while placing the mudrā upon the crown of the head.
Visualize the mudrā as the form of the Buddha.
Next, bind the Samaya-mudrā of the Lotus Family:
join both hands as before in *añjali* and slightly open them.
The two middle fingers advance two finger-widths, with the tips of the two joints slightly curved;
their heads are separated by approximately one cun each.
The two index fingers and the two ring fingers are both held together and upright.
Forming the shape of a blooming lotus flower,
recite the mantra three times; then,
raising the mudrā, place it upon the right side of the crown of the head, above the right ear.
Visualize yourself as Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
The Lotus Samaya Mantra is:
Oṃ paṇamu nābhavāya svāhā. Next, bind the Vajra-kula Samaya-mudrā.
As before, perform the universal prostration and place the mudrā at the heart;
recite the mantra three times.
Then, raise the mudrā and place it upon the left ear above the crown of the head.
Visualize yourself as Vajragarbha Bodhisattva.
The Samaya-mantra of the Vajra Family is:
Oṃ vāyudhānavadya svāhā. With this, perform the seal for protecting the body.
The two hands are positioned with the right pressing upon the left;
the fingers are interlaced within and held straight upward,
with the two thumbs pressed against each other.
The two concentrations are slightly curved;
at their two ends they turn away so as not to touch each other,
resembling the shape of a three-pronged ritual mace (triśūla).
Place both hands together with the palms facing upward;
by pressing the two thumbs against the second phalanges of the index fingers, the seal is formed.
In this sūtra, it is also permissible to use the root mudrā instead.
Now, taking the general dhāraṇī-mantras from the Susiddhikara-sūtra, they are not [to be recited] with the *vajra* (crossed) fingers.
The mantra for protecting the body is:
Oṃ sarva-ṣṭhāva-śaṅkarakaṇi-kuru-dhāra-kṣara-kṣara-maḥ svāhā. By means of this, one should form this mudrā.
Recite the preceding mantra and consecrate five places on one's own body:
first the forehead, then the right shoulder, the left shoulder, the heart, and the throat.
These are the five places.
By empowering one's own body through the power of the mantra,
one immediately becomes clad in the adamantine armor.
Next, perform the mudrā for expelling all obstacles and binding the vināyakas:
interlace the ten fingers of both hands with the palms facing inward; bend the two thumbs into the palms;
and with the nails turned away from each other, pinch the surfaces of the two index fingers.
Quickly clench your fists and visualize Vināyakas;
all those who create obstacles and difficulties shall be bound with the fivefold fetters.
The mantra for expelling obstacles is:
Oṃ duna viduna trāśaya śodhaya sarvavighnān hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Next, bind the seal of the Vajra Armor.
Then, with the previous mudrā, straighten the two thumbs so that their tips touch one another.
With the two index fingers, pinch the first joint of the lower part of each thumb; thus the mudrā is formed.
Use this mudrā as before to consecrate five locations on one’s own body.
The entire body is spontaneously clad in adamantine armor, its radiance blazing brilliantly.
The mantra is:
Oṃ hṛīḥ kaṇaye mānaha hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Next, form the seal of the adamantine wall.
This is the same as the previous Armor Mudrā;
however, open the two thumbs,
keeping them about one inch apart.
Open the palms in the shape of a wall and it is accomplished.
The mantra is:
Oṃ hrīḥ kaṇi naha naha paca paca hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. With this mudrā, place it upon the crown of the head.
Circumambulate three times to the right in mid-air while reciting the mantra three times;
by the power of this empowerment and its majestic spiritual force, [the rite is accomplished].
Surrounding the four directions,
one forms a vajra wall at whatever distance the mind intends;
each boundary shines with radiant light.
All māras dare not approach or draw near.
Next, perform the mudrā for inviting the Honored Sage:
interlace the two hands with the palms facing inward and extend the fingers straight upward.
Second, the pillar of the head of meditative concentration:
beckon it toward the body with the two wisdom hands.
The mantra for inviting the Honored One is as follows:
Oṃ dūṇibhaga vaṃ vṛścikaṇi rudre he hūṃ phaṭ. Do not alter this mudrā.
Then, recite the subsequent mantra for inviting the Noble Lord and his retinue:
Oṃ saparivāram āvāhaya bhagavan kuru dharmam anusmara svāhā. Next, form the mudrā of the Wrathful King of All Mantras, Caṇḍa-muṇḍa.
Having expelled all demons and fears, they remain hidden among the assembly of noble ones;
by the majestic power of the Vidyārāja, he searches through the rafters and dispatches them away,
leaving behind only those who create obstacles for the noble ones and their own retinues.
For this mudrā, join the two *śraddhā* (faith) fingers by crossing the right over the left and tucking them inside;
join the two *vīrya* (diligence) fingers by bending them double and placing them side-by-side over the crossed *śraddhā* fingers;
and place the two *smṛti* (mindfulness) fingers upright with their tips touching.
Because the two meditative concentrations are each slightly curved,
they do not touch one another behind the two recollections,
resembling the shape of a three-pronged vajra.
With both hands held upright and the two index fingers extended upward, the mudrā is formed.
While reciting the mantra,
rotate the mudrā three times counter-clockwise in the air.
Having expelled and banished the treacherous māras,
he immediately circumambulated three times to the right,
thereby forming a vajra-light, adamantine great boundary.
Because all ordinary beings and sages alike must not transgress this boundary;
those who do so will find that their samaya is rendered unstable by the transformative power [of the deities],
and they shall incur the secret punishment of the assembly of sages for such transgression.
This is because it is the solemn vow of all the holy ones.
Then he recited the mantra of Kuṇḍalī, saying:
*Namo ratnatrayāya, namo śrīvajra...* (Namo ratnatrayāya, namo śrīvajra).
VAJRAPRACANDĀYE MAHĀYAKṢASENĀPATE OM AMṚTAKUNDALI KṢA KṢA KHA KHĪ KHA KHĪ TIṢṬHA TIṢṬHA.
Hana hana daha daha jvala jvala visphoṭaya visphoṭaya sarvavighnān vināśaya mahāgrahanivartani vidrāvaya hūṃ.
With the *phaṭ* syllable, one immediately forms the Vajra-net mudrā of the upper direction;
this is the same as the previous wall mudrā,
formed by spreading the two wisdom fingers and holding them straight upright.
Place the mudrā upon the crown of the head, circling it three times to the right;
by reciting the mantra three times, it is accomplished,
and a vajra-net completely covers its surface.
The mantra is:
Oṃ vajrapañjara hūṃ phaṭ. Next, perform the mudrā for offering the arghya perfumed water to bathe the Honored One.
Using the aforementioned seal for invitation,
join the two wisdom fingers so that each grasps the first joint below the root of the two concentration fingers;
place the seal at the heart.
The base is flat and wide, shaped like a shallow cup.
Hold the seal at the level of the forehead as an offering.
If there is a vessel for fragrant water, [use it].
Then, press it with this mudrā.
Recite the mantra three times or once,
and thereafter hold it up and offer it.
The mantra is:
Oṃ vāyurnāga hūṃ. Next, form the seal of the Jewel Mountain using the single-pronged vajra seal.
The upper joint is level like the shape of the crown of the head.
By placing two *śrī* (惠) fingers upright and pressing down upon the various fingers in the palm, it is completed.
Recite the *Ratnakoṭi* (寶山) mantra as follows:
Oṃ aśara hūṃ. Next, perform the mudrā for the lotus seat:
using the previous *argha* mudrā, extend both thumbs outward and hold them upright.
They are separated by a distance of about half an inch and are shaped like lotus flowers.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ vajravīraya svāhā. Next, present the five offerings. First, form the mudrā of scented unguent (*gandha*), which is the same as the previously mentioned single-pronged vajra mudrā.
With the two thumbs slightly bent,
pinch the first joint of the two index fingers downward;
when they are separated by about one cun, it is complete.
The mantra for the scented ointment is:
Oṃ kaṇi-kuru dhā sarva-sattva-puṣpa-kara rakṣa rakṣa sarva-jñāni svāhā. Next, form the mudrā for offering flowers.
This is the same as the previously described single-pronged vajra mudrā;
by extending the right hand in the gesture of generosity, it is perfected.
Recite the Flower Offering Mantra, saying:
Oṃ kaṇi puṣpa muṣṇāpaya hūṃ. Next, form the incense mudrā:
it is the same as the previous single-pronged mudrā, with the left hand extended downward; thus it is accomplished.
Recite the incense mantra:
Oṃ kaṇi kuru dhūpa-dhūpeṣṭa-ruṭ-kṛta pūra-vaktra-grahana-grahana dūṣaṇa svāhā. Next, form the mudrā for offering food.
Following the previous method for the single-pronged vajra mudrā,
extend the two index fingers and the two little fingers so their tips touch,
while the remaining four fingers are interlaced within to form fists; thus it is completed.
The mantra is:
Oṃ kaṇi hūṃ hūṃ svāhā. Next, form the lamp-light mudrā, which is the same as the previously described single-pronged vajra mudrā.
The two hands, with palms facing the body and fingers extended upward, are joined together.
Recite the Dīpa-prakāśa mantra:
Oṃ kaṇi ni-paṇi-pāya hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Next, bind the seal of universal offering (samantapūjā-mudrā).
Join the two hands in *añjali*.
Press the right hand over the left, interlacing the fingers so that the first joints are crossed.
From this mudrā, one should visualize [light] flowing forth.
Various offerings transformed into clouds and oceans of seven-jeweled palaces and towers; clothing,
food, drink, and exquisite celestial music filled the entire dharma-realm.
I make offerings to all the noble assembly.
Now, I shall briefly cite one or two examples;
were I to explain them in detail:
As stated in the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*,
one should perform the offering by reciting this offering mantra three or seven times.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ amoghapāśa-padmajvala-pratīcchaya hūṃ jjaḥ. Having thus performed all these offerings:
Whirling the vajra with the right hand,
recite the root mantra before the assembly of holy beings.
Visualize yourself as being face-to-face with the Supreme One;
assume the posture of a dancing trample,
emulating Vajrasattva.
Before the Tathāgata,
he brandished and tossed his vajra,
and by means of this, empowered his own five places.
With the left hand, one grasps the vajra bell and shakes it three times before the forehead.
This symbolizes making offerings to the noble assembly with the sounds of celestial music, causing them to rejoice.
One should also recite the root mantra while the mind abides in the sublime samādhi of the sattva; above this, one employs the two mantras and mudrās of the bell and vajra,
which have been transmitted through the secret lineage of the masters from of old and are not recorded in written texts.
Human wisdom is limited; thus,
some transmissions may be incomplete,
or those who receive them may lack clarity, resulting in the proliferation of various versions.
The sequence and details differ;

I have therefore recorded this as a draft for future reference. Furthermore, practitioners should take care that amidst their service and offerings, there may be no forgetfulness, errors, omissions, or violations of the *samaya* precepts.
If there are karmic obstacles from offenses committed over many lifetimes that have not yet been eliminated,
one should recite the hundred-syllable mantra of the Vajra Family to compensate for them and to secretly extinguish all such transgressions.
One attains purity of body and mind and becomes in accord with the Dharma.
The hundred-syllable mantra is as follows:
Oṃ vajrasattva samayam anupālaya vajrasattva tvenopatiṣṭha dṛḍho me bhava.
*Om ambe ambike 'mbālike na māṇiye svāhā.
Ambe ambike 'mbālike na māṇiye svāhā. Anuṣvare kumārī-bhaṭṭārike svāhā.
Su-puṣṭe svāhā. Sarva-siddhiṃ me prayaccha svāhā.*
HŪṂ SVĀHĀ SARVA KARMASU CA ME RĀGACCHIRA YOGA RO HŪṂ HA HA HA HA HOḤ SAGHAṂ SARVATATHĀGATA VAJRĀBHISHEKAṂ.
15. On the left, *vaḥ* and *dharī*; 16. *mahāsamayasattvāya*;
17. *hrīḥ*. For this mudrā, the two hands are joined with the right over the left.
Cross the hands externally to form fists with the middle fingers extended straight upward and joined together;
this is called the Samaya-mudrā.
By forming this mudrā,
apply it to four places on the body:
the heart, the forehead, the throat, and the crown of the head.
Furthermore, by reciting the hundred-syllable mantra,
one can eliminate all grave sins accumulated since beginningless time,
including the offenses of violating the four grave prohibitions, committing the five acts of immediate retribution, and slandering the Vaipulya sutras.
All such sins as these shall be completely extinguished;
how much more so minor transgressions committed through negligence that would not otherwise be purified?
Thereupon, one should form the mudrā of the Honored One.
Join the two hands in *añjali*.
Place the two ring fingers with the left one positioned in front at the bottom and the right one positioned behind at the top.
Cross the backs of the left ring fingers; then,
behind the backs of the two middle fingers,
hook the tips of both index fingers around the tips of the two ring fingers respectively.
The two middle fingers are held together and upright;
the two thumbs are likewise held together and upright,
pressing against the middle joints of the two middle fingers.
Joining the two little fingers together and holding them upright,
the seal is formed. Recite the root mantra and apply the seal to four places on the body.
The mantra is as follows:
*Namo ratnatrayāya, namo vajrapāṇaye mahāyakṣasenāpataye tadyathā oṃ kaṇi duni hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. Furthermore, one should form the second root mudrā.
This is the same as the aforementioned initial mudrā for protecting the body;
it is also called the single-pronged vajra mudrā.
This is identical to the mudrā of the Bodhisattva Tārā.
The second root mantra is as follows:
*Namo ratnatrayāya, namo vajrapāṇaye mahāyakṣasenāpataye tadyathā | oṃ duna viduna kaṇi kuru dhā sarvārthāni hūṃ*. Next, perform the head mudrā.
This is the same as the previous single-pronged vajra mudrā;
however, with the two thumbs, each hook the tips of the two ring fingers,
and by pressing them against the inner side of their upper joints within the palms, it is formed.
The mantra is:
Oṃ hūṃ hūṃ mama phaṭ. Next, form the *mūrdha-mudrā* (crown seal), which is the same as the previously mentioned single-pronged vajra seal.
It is formed by holding the two thumbs upright and pressing them against each other.
The mantra is:
Oṃ hṛīḥ caṇḍakani naha pāśa hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Fourth, bind the heart mudrā.
Then, place the aforementioned root mudrā upon the heart and empower it once with the heart mantra.
The mantra is:
Oṃ kaṇi hūṃ phaṭ. Next, holding the rosary at the heart, empower it seven times with the随心真言 (Sui-xin zhenyan / *Cittānugata-mantra*).
The mantra is:
Oṃ kaṇi duma bi hūṃ phaṭ (with the *phaṭ* pronounced as a single mora).
Placing both hands at the heart, holding the rosary, one should recite while sitting upright with a dignified posture and focused, earnest contemplation.
The mind abides in the sublime visualization of the majestic power of the deity,
which is neither identical to nor different from the painted image, like a form reflected in a mirror.
Pure and free from blemish,
one contemplates external majestic radiance while the mind abides in the sublime contemplation of loving-kindness and compassion.
Taking pity on the various classes of beings within the six realms of existence who wander incessantly through the four modes of birth,
I now give rise to a mind of fierce, sharp, and courageous faith,
and with utmost sincerity, I recite these wondrous and sublime verses.
The mind abides in the wisdom-visualization of the yoga of the deity.
Now that my body and mind have attained purity,
I dedicate this merit and its spiritual power to pervade the entire realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu).
Universally saving all sentient beings,
may they, through this empowerment,
all become like my own body.
If one follows the original sūtra,
there are fifteen additional paths;
the mantras and mudrās should be recited and practiced in their entirety.
One should ensure that they become thoroughly proficient,
so that when the time comes for them to be applied in accordance with the task at hand,
they may be employed to prepare for urgent difficulties as they arise.
It serves to supplement what is lacking and is not an item for ordinary daily use;
this is stated in the Great Sūtra.
This shall not be recounted again;
should you require it when facing a specific matter,
you may consult and apply it yourself.

This ritual manual for the recitation and offering of Mahākrodhavajrakumāra was transcribed by another hand in the seventh month of the third year of the Reki-ō era, so that the Dharma may endure for a long time.
One Seal Transmission: The *Siddhi-vajra-sūtra*, Volume 58, Section 5.8.
